question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

A person who prevents others from enjoying something that he himself cannot use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A dog in the manger.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "a dog in the manger" describes a person who selfishly keeps others from having or enjoying something that he himself has no use for. (कुत्ते की तरह स्वयं न खाना और न दूसरों को खाने देना)
◦ Example: He will not use the spare room himself and will not let anyone else use it either — a perfect dog in the manger.

 

• The expression comes from one of Aesop's fables, in which a dog lies in a manger full of hay and growls at the cattle that come to eat, though he cannot eat the hay himself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: To let sleeping dogs lie (सोए हुए मामले को न छेड़ना): To avoid reopening a settled quarrel or an old problem.

 

• Option 2: Dog days (भीषण गर्मी के दिन): The hottest days of summer, so called from the rising of the Dog Star, Sirius, at that season.

 

• Option 4: To go to the dogs (बर्बाद हो जाना): To decline sharply, to fall into ruin.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "dog" idioms frequently asked: "A dog's life" (a life of misery), "To rain cats and dogs" (to rain heavily), "Every dog has its day" (everyone gets a chance sooner or later), "To be dog-tired" and "The tail wagging the dog".

 

• Related idioms of selfishness: "To look after number one" and "To feather one's own nest".

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To pay an unreasonably high price for something.
option_1: To look down one's nose at
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To pay through the nose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "to pay through the nose" means to pay a great deal more for something than it is worth. (मुँहमाँगी कीमत चुकाना)
◦ Example: Travellers who arrive without a booking often have to pay through the nose for a room.

 

• The four options are all built on the word "nose", and the question therefore tests the candidate's ability to distinguish between idioms drawn from a single word-family.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: To look down one's nose at (हेय दृष्टि से देखना): To regard somebody or something with contempt.

 

• Option 2: To keep one's nose clean (मुसीबत से दूर रहना): To stay out of trouble and avoid doing anything wrong.

 

• Option 4: To poke one's nose into (दूसरों के मामलों में दखल देना): To interfere in matters that are not one's concern.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "nose" idioms: "Under one's nose" (right in front of somebody), "To turn up one's nose at" (to reject scornfully), "To lead somebody by the nose" (to control completely), "To win by a nose" (to win by a very narrow margin) and "As plain as the nose on your face".

 

• Related idioms about cost: "To cost an arm and a leg", "To break the bank" and "A king's ransom".

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rhythm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Rhythm" — a regular repeated pattern of sound, movement or events. (लय / ताल)
◦ Example: The dancers moved in perfect rhythm with the drums.

 

• Spelling key: the word contains two "h"s and no true vowel except the "y" — RH-Y-THM. It is of Greek origin, from *rhythmos*, and the "rh" at the beginning is the mark of that origin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Rythm" — incorrect; the first "h" has been dropped.

 

• Option 2: "Rhythem" — incorrect; an "e" has been wrongly inserted before the final "m".

 

• Option 4: "Rythem" — incorrect on both counts.

 

NOTE

 

• Other Greek-derived words beginning with "rh": rhetoric, rhinoceros, rheumatism, rhapsody, rhombus and rhododendron.

 

• Words in which "y" functions as the only vowel: rhythm, myth, gym, hymn, lynx, crypt and syzygy.

 

• The related adjective is rhythmic and the adverb rhythmically.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Guarantee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Guarantee" — a formal assurance that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if faulty. (गारंटी / प्रत्याभूति)
◦ Example: The appliance carries a two-year guarantee against manufacturing defects.

 

• Spelling key: GUA + RAN + TEE. The word begins with "gua", like guard and guardian, has a single "r", and ends in "-tee".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Gurantee" — incorrect; the "a" after "gu" has been dropped.

 

• Option 2: "Guarrantee" — incorrect; the "r" has been wrongly doubled.

 

• Option 4: "Garantee" — incorrect; the "u" has been dropped.

 

NOTE

 

• Note the related word "guarantor" — the person who gives a guarantee — and the distinction between guarantee (the assurance itself, and the commoner spelling) and guaranty, a term now confined to legal usage.

 

• Other words beginning with the silent "gu": guard, guardian, guess, guest, guide, guild, guilt and guitar.

 

• The word is of French origin and is related to warranty, which comes from the same root through a different line of descent.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

The soldiers held the garrisson against repeated attacks for three weeks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. garrison.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "garrisson", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "garrison" — with a double "r" and a single "s". (सैनिक छावनी / रक्षक सेना)

 

• A "garrison" is a body of troops stationed in a fortress or town to defend it, and also the building or post itself.
◦ Example: A small garrison was left behind to hold the fort.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The soldiers held the garrison against repeated attacks for three weeks.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "garisson" — incorrect; the doubling has been transferred from the "r" to the "s".

 

• Option 3: "garison" — incorrect; neither letter has been doubled.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because the given word is misspelt and does require replacement.

 

NOTE

 

• Military terms with tricky spellings, frequently tested in SSC: garrison, battalion, regiment, cavalry, artillery, infantry, barracks, reconnaissance, siege, guerrilla, lieutenant, colonel and sergeant.

 

• Note the useful distinction: a cantonment is a permanent military station, a garrison the troops stationed there, and a barrack the building in which they are housed.

question: Choose the word that is the most appropriate synonym of the word "seldom".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rarely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Seldom" is an adverb of frequency meaning not often; on very few occasions. (कदाचित् / विरले ही)
◦ Example: He seldom speaks in the meetings, though he listens with great attention.

 

• "Rarely" carries exactly this sense and is therefore the closest synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Often (प्रायः), Option 2: Always (हमेशा) and Option 4: Frequently (बार-बार) all denote high frequency, and are therefore antonyms of seldom rather than synonyms.

 

NOTE

 

• Adverbs of frequency arranged from the most to the least frequent: always → usually → often/frequently → sometimes → occasionally → seldom/rarely → hardly ever → never.

 

• An important grammatical point: seldom, rarely, hardly, scarcely and never are negative in force, and must not be used with another negative. *He seldom ever comes* is acceptable, but *He does not seldom come* is wrong.

 

• When a sentence begins with any of these words, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: *Seldom have I seen such a performance.*

question:
Choose the correct synonym for the underlined word in the following sentence.

The committee decided to postpone the hearing until the following month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Defer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Postpone" means to put off an event to a later time. (स्थगित करना)
◦ Example: The match was postponed on account of rain.

 

• "Defer" means exactly the same — to delay something until a later date — and is therefore the correct synonym.
◦ Example: The decision on the matter was deferred to the next meeting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Cancel (रद्द करना): To call something off altogether, so that it does not take place at all. This is the sharpest distractor, because both words concern an event that will not happen as planned — but a postponed event is merely moved, while a cancelled one is abandoned.

 

• Option 2: Conclude (समाप्त करना): To bring to an end.

 

• Option 3: Advance (पहले करना): To move something to an earlier date — the exact opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of postpone: Defer, Adjourn, Put off, Shelve, Suspend, Prorogue, Hold over.

 

• Note the parliamentary distinctions, frequently tested: adjournment suspends a sitting for a specified time; adjournment sine die ends it for an indefinite period; prorogation ends a session; and dissolution ends the life of the House.

question: Which of the following words is the closest synonym of the word "immense"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Enormous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Immense" means extremely large in size, extent or degree; vast. (विशाल / अपार)
◦ Example: The project required an immense amount of labour and money.

 

• "Enormous" carries the same sense of very great size or quantity, and is therefore the closest synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three remaining alternatives — tiny (अत्यंत छोटा), average (औसत) and narrow (संकीर्ण) — are all opposed in sense to *immense*, and none of them can serve as its synonym.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of immense: Enormous, Vast, Colossal, Gigantic, Prodigious, Mammoth, Stupendous, Immeasurable.

 

• Antonyms: Minute, Diminutive, Meagre, Negligible, Paltry, Insignificant.

 

• The word comes from the Latin *im-* (not) and *mensus* (measured) — literally, that which cannot be measured. The related noun is immensity.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "artificial".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Natural.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Artificial" means made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally; also, insincere or affected in manner. (कृत्रिम / बनावटी)
◦ Example: The lake is artificial and was created by damming the stream.

 

• "Natural" means existing in or produced by nature, without human intervention, and is therefore the correct antonym. (प्राकृतिक)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Synthetic (कृत्रिम / संश्लेषित): Made by chemical synthesis rather than obtained from nature — a synonym of artificial.

 

• Option 2: Manufactured (निर्मित): Made by machinery on a large scale — also a synonym in this context.

 

• Option 3: Imitation (नकली): Made to resemble something more valuable — again close in sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Note the contrasting pairs frequently tested in science and geography: natural fibres (cotton, silk, wool, jute) and synthetic fibres (nylon, rayon, polyester, acrylic); natural rubber and synthetic rubber; natural satellite (the Moon) and artificial satellite (Aryabhata, INSAT).

 

• Synonyms of natural: Innate, Inherent, Instinctive, Unaffected, Spontaneous, Genuine.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "permanent".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Temporary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Permanent" means lasting or intended to last indefinitely, without change. (स्थायी)
◦ Example: He was confirmed in a permanent post after two years of probation.

 

• "Temporary" means lasting for only a limited time, and is therefore the correct antonym. (अस्थायी)
◦ Example: A temporary bridge was thrown across the river during the repairs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Lasting (टिकाऊ) and Option 2: Enduring (चिरस्थायी) both denote continuance over a long period — synonyms of permanent.

 

• Option 4: Perpetual (शाश्वत): Never ending or changing — again a synonym, and indeed a stronger one.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of permanent: Everlasting, Abiding, Immutable, Indelible, Fixed, Stable.

 

• Synonyms of temporary: Transient, Transitory, Ephemeral, Fleeting, Provisional, Interim, Makeshift.

 

• Note the useful institutional contrast: the Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved, while the Lok Sabha has a fixed term of five years.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of "Barren".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fertile.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Barren" means land that is too poor to produce vegetation or crops; unproductive. (बंजर / ऊसर)
◦ Example: Years of over-cultivation had left the fields barren.

 

• "Fertile" means capable of producing abundant vegetation or crops; rich and productive, and is therefore the correct antonym. (उपजाऊ)
◦ Example: The alluvial soil of the Ganga plain is extremely fertile.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Desolate (उजाड़): Deserted and bleak — again close in sense.

 

• Option 2: Arid (शुष्क): Extremely dry, having little or no rainfall — a synonym of barren in the geographical sense.

 

• Option 4: Sterile (बंध्य / निर्जीव): Unable to produce offspring or crops; also free from bacteria — a synonym of barren.

 

NOTE

 

• Note the figurative uses, which are equally common: "a barren discussion" means one that leads to no result, while "a fertile imagination" means an inventive one.

 

• Synonyms of fertile: Productive, Fruitful, Prolific, Rich, Luxuriant, Fecund.

 

• In geography, alluvial soil is the most fertile in India, and laterite soil among the least fertile without treatment.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is easily deceived or cheated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Gullible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Gullible" describes a person who is easily persuaded to believe something, and is therefore easily deceived or cheated. (भोला / आसानी से बहकने वाला)
◦ Example: The scheme succeeded because it preyed upon gullible investors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Shrewd (चतुर / व्यावहारिक बुद्धिमान): Having sharp practical judgement — the opposite of gullible.

 

• Option 2: Vigilant (सतर्क): Watchful and alert against danger.

 

• Option 3: Cunning (धूर्त): Skilled at deceiving others, which is the reverse of being deceived oneself.

 

NOTE

 

• Related one-word substitutions for kinds of persons: Credulous (too ready to believe — very close to gullible), Sceptic (one who habitually doubts), Cynic (one who believes people act only from self-interest), Naive (lacking experience), Astute (shrewd and discerning) and Charlatan (one who falsely claims special knowledge).

 

• Note the distinction between gullible and credulous: both denote readiness to believe, but *gullible* stresses the resulting exploitation, while *credulous* stresses the belief itself.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is shrewd and cannot easily be deceived.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Astute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Astute" describes a person of sharp practical judgement, quick to see an advantage and difficult to deceive. (कुशाग्रबुद्धि / चतुर)
◦ Example: He proved an astute negotiator and secured very favourable terms.

 

• The word carries a note of approval — it praises the shrewdness of a person, unlike *cunning*, which implies deceit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Gullible (भोला): Easily deceived — the exact opposite of astute.

 

• Option 2: Naive (अनुभवहीन / सरल): Lacking experience and judgement, and therefore easily imposed upon.

 

• Option 4: Credulous (जल्दी विश्वास कर लेने वाला): Too ready to believe what one is told — again the opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of astute: Shrewd, Perceptive, Discerning, Sagacious, Canny, Judicious, Perspicacious.

 

• Note the shades of meaning within this group: astute and shrewd praise practical sharpness; sagacious and judicious suggest wisdom and sound judgement; cunning, crafty and wily carry disapproval, since they imply the use of that sharpness to deceive.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who is slow to understand and dull in perception.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Obtuse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obtuse" describes a person who is slow to understand, dull of perception and insensitive to what is going on around him. (मंदबुद्धि / कुंठित)
◦ Example: He was too obtuse to notice that his remarks had given offence.

 

• The word comes from the Latin *obtusus*, meaning blunted — the same root that gives the geometrical obtuse angle, an angle greater than 90° and therefore "blunt" as against the "sharp" acute angle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Acute (तीक्ष्ण): Sharp and penetrating in mind or in the senses — the direct opposite of obtuse, in both the ordinary and the geometrical sense.

 

• Option 2: Astute (कुशाग्रबुद्धि): Shrewd and quick in practical judgement — an antonym.

 

• Option 3: Perceptive (सूक्ष्मदर्शी): Quick to notice and understand things — again an antonym.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of obtuse: Dull, Slow-witted, Dim, Insensitive, Imperceptive, Thick.

 

• Antonyms: Astute, Sharp, Shrewd, Perceptive, Discerning, Quick-witted.

 

• Note the parallel between the two senses of the word: acute and obtuse are opposites both in geometry, where they describe sharp and blunt angles, and in ordinary speech, where they describe sharp and blunt minds.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The chairman was averse ______ any change in the existing rules of the society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "averse" is followed by the preposition "to", meaning strongly disinclined towards or opposed to something. (विमुख / अनिच्छुक)
◦ Example: He is not averse to a little hard work.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The chairman was averse to any change in the existing rules of the society.*

 

• A useful group to learn together, all of which take "to" and denote inclination or its absence: averse to, indifferent to, partial to, addicted to, accustomed to, prone to, susceptible to and liable to.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "from" is the commonest error here, by confusion with the noun "aversion", which may take either "to" or "from" — but the adjective averse takes only "to".

 

• Option 3: "for" is used with "eager for", "anxious for", "famous for" and "eligible for".

 

• Option 4: "with" is used with "familiar with", "satisfied with" and "popular with".

 

NOTE

 

• Note the distinction between "averse" (disinclined, of a person) and "adverse" (unfavourable, of circumstances) — *adverse weather*, *adverse remarks*, but *averse to travel*. The two are constantly confused in examinations.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The scheme was implemented ______ accordance with the guidelines issued by the ministry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed prepositional phrase is "in accordance with", meaning in a manner conforming to a rule, order or wish. (के अनुसार / के अनुरूप)
◦ Example: The appointment was made in accordance with the recruitment rules.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The scheme was implemented in accordance with the guidelines issued by the ministry.*

 

• Note that the phrase is always followed by "with", never by "to" — *in accordance with the rules*, not "in accordance to the rules".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "on" appears in "on the basis of", "on behalf of" and "on account of".

 

• Option 2: "by" appears in "by virtue of", "by means of" and "by dint of".

 

• Option 4: "at" appears in "at the instance of" and "at the behest of".

 

NOTE

 

• Other fixed phrases beginning with "in", frequently tested in SSC: in comparison with/to, in conformity with, in compliance with, in consonance with, in pursuance of, in lieu of, in the event of, in respect of, in view of, in spite of and in the wake of.

 

• Note the closely related pair: "in accordance with" (following a rule) and "according to" (as stated by a person or source) — *according to the newspaper*, but *in accordance with the law*.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The clock tower had been silent for as long as most of the town could remember.

A. A watchmaker from the next district was persuaded to come and look at it.

B. He spent four days inside the tower with a lamp and a bag of tools.

C. Then, one morning, the municipality found a small sum in its accounts that had no other claim on it.

D. On the fifth morning the bell struck seven, and half the town stopped in the street.

S2. It has kept time ever since, and nobody now remembers the years of silence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. CABD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – C – A – B – D – S2, moving from the means → the man → the work → the result.

 

• S1 → C: S1 states that the clock had long been silent. C begins with "Then, one morning", a marker of the change that breaks the deadlock — the municipality finds the money. Nothing could be done until funds were available, so C must come first.

 

• C → A: A follows naturally — with money in hand, a watchmaker is persuaded to come. The engagement of a craftsman presupposes the means of paying him.

 

• A → B: B begins with the pronoun "He", which refers to the watchmaker of A, and describes his four days of work inside the tower.

 

• B → D: D speaks of "the fifth morning", a date reckoned from the four days of B. This numerical link fixes the order beyond dispute.

 

• D → S2: S2 records that the clock has kept time ever since, following directly from the striking of the bell in D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ABCD) is incorrect on both counts, and it also strands C in the middle of the narrative.

 

• Option 2 (ACBD) is incorrect because the watchmaker could not be engaged (A) before the money had been found (C).

 

• Option 3 (CBAD) is incorrect because B opens with "He", and the pronoun has no antecedent until A introduces the watchmaker.

 

NOTE

 

• Two clues settle this question: the pronoun "He" in B, which must follow the naming of a person; and the phrase "the fifth morning" in D, which must be counted from the four days mentioned in B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. My mother measured everything by hand.

A. A pinch of this and a fistful of that, and never a spoon in sight.

B. When I asked her for a recipe she could give me only the names of the ingredients.

C. I have her handwriting on a dozen scraps of paper, and not one quantity among them.

D. The quantities, she said, were in the fingers, and could not be written down.

S2. Her cooking, I have come to understand, was never meant to be copied, only remembered.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ABDC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – A – B – D – C – S2, moving from the habit → the request → her reply → its consequence.

 

• S1 → A: S1 states that the mother measured everything by hand. A illustrates that statement directly — a pinch of this, a fistful of that, and never a spoon. An illustration follows the claim it illustrates.

 

• A → B: B introduces the narrator's request for a recipe, and reports that she could give only the names of the ingredients — the natural consequence of measuring by hand.

 

• B → D: D gives her explanation, in her own words: the quantities were in the fingers and could not be written down. An explanation must follow the situation it accounts for.

 

• D → C: C describes what the narrator is left with — a dozen scraps of paper with names and "not one quantity among them". This is the direct result of what D has just explained.

 

• C → S2: S2 draws the reflection that the cooking was never meant to be copied, only remembered — which follows from the absence of quantities in C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BADC) is incorrect because A illustrates S1 and should follow it immediately, before the narrative moves to the request in B.

 

• Option 3 (ADBC) is incorrect because D is her reply, and a reply cannot precede the request made in B.

 

• Option 4 (BDAC) is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1, and it separates A from the statement it illustrates.

 

NOTE

 

• A useful principle for descriptive paragraphs: a general statement is followed by its illustration, and only then does the narrative move forward. Sentences reporting speech — here *"The quantities, she said…"* — must follow whatever prompted that speech.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The postman's bicycle had no bell.

A. Instead he whistled the first line of an old film song as he turned into the lane.

B. Every household knew the tune, and knew what it meant.

C. Doors opened before he had reached them.

D. In thirty years he never once changed the song.

S2. When he retired at last, the lane stayed shut in the mornings for a long while afterwards.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ABCD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – A – B – C – D – S2, moving from the substitute for the bell → its recognition → its effect → its constancy.

 

• S1 → A: S1 states that the bicycle had no bell. A begins with the word "Instead", which points directly back to that absence and supplies what took its place — the whistled tune. This is a mandatory pair.

 

• A → B: B speaks of "the tune", using the definite article, which presupposes the tune introduced in A. Every household knew it and knew what it meant.

 

• B → C: C gives the effect of that recognition — doors opened before he reached them. Recognition must precede the response.

 

• C → D: D adds the final touch, that in thirty years he never changed the song. It explains how the tune came to be so universally known, and rounds off the description.

 

• D → S2: S2 records his retirement and the silence that followed, which follows naturally from the thirty years of D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BACD) is incorrect because B refers to "the tune", which has not yet been mentioned; A must introduce it first.

 

• Option 2 (ABDC) is incorrect because it places the constancy of the song (D) before its effect (C), breaking the chain of recognition and response.

 

• Option 4 (BADC) is incorrect on both counts.

 

NOTE

 

• The word "Instead" is among the most decisive clues in para-jumbles. It always refers back to something that did not happen or was absent, and the sentence containing it must follow that statement immediately.

question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options 1, 2 or 3 do not improve the sentence, then choose Option 4: "No improvement required."

The whole department was taken by surprised when the transfer orders were announced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. by surprise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct idiom is "to take somebody by surprise", meaning to happen unexpectedly and catch a person unprepared. (अचानक चौंका देना)
◦ Example: The announcement took everyone by surprise.

 

• The error in the given sentence is one of word form: "surprised" is a past participle used as an adjective, whereas the idiom requires the noun "surprise" after the preposition "by".

 

• The improved sentence reads: *The whole department was taken by surprise when the transfer orders were announced.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "with surprise" is possible in other constructions — *He looked at me with surprise* — but it does not fit the fixed idiom *take by surprise*.

 

• Option 3: "in surprise" is likewise used elsewhere — *She stepped back in surprise* — but not with the verb *take*.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because the sentence does contain an error.

 

NOTE

 

• Other fixed expressions with "by" in which a noun must follow: by chance, by mistake, by accident, by force, by heart, by turns, by degrees, by all means, by no means and by and large.

 

• Note the related idioms of the unexpected: "To catch somebody off guard", "To spring a surprise on" and "Out of the blue".

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on the passage.

 

The habit of asking where a piece of information comes from is now so ordinary that it seems to need no explanation. As a formal method of study, however, it is barely two centuries old. Its founder is usually taken to be Leopold von Ranke (1795-1886), who insisted that history should be written not from the chronicles of later writers but from the documents of the period itself — from letters, dispatches, treaties and the records of governments.
Ranke's method was called scientific, and the description was not merely flattering. What made it so was that its results could in principle be checked. Any reader could return to the same archive, consult the same file, and judge for himself whether the historian had read it correctly. A conclusion that rested on the authority of the historian alone was, on this view, no conclusion at all.
His pupils carried the method into the universities of Europe and then of America, where the seminar — a small class working directly on original documents — became the standard form of training. Within a generation the writing of history had been transformed from a branch of literature into a discipline with a technique that could be taught.
The method has not gone unquestioned. Its critics observe that archives preserve what governments chose to keep, and that a history built on official papers will inevitably be a history of officials. The remedy proposed has not been to abandon the method but to widen the range of what counts as a document — to admit private letters, account books, photographs, oral testimony and the evidence of objects.

 

According to the passage, what did Ranke insist that history should be written from?
option_1: The chronicles compiled by later writers
option_2: The documents of the period itself, such as letters, dispatches and treaties
option_3: The personal recollections of the historian
option_4: Works of imaginative literature of the period
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The documents of the period itself, such as letters, dispatches and treaties.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage states it directly: Ranke *"insisted that history should be written not from the chronicles of later writers but from the documents of the period itself — from letters, dispatches, treaties and the records of governments."*

 

• The distinction is between a secondary source — an account written afterwards by somebody who was not present — and a primary source, produced at the time by those involved. Ranke's whole method rests on the preference for the second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is the very thing Ranke rejected, and is offered in the passage only to be set aside.

 

• Option 3 is contradicted by the second paragraph, which says that a conclusion resting on the historian's own authority is "no conclusion at all".

 

• Option 4 is not mentioned; imaginative literature forms no part of Ranke's prescribed material.

 

NOTE

 

• Where a passage uses the construction "not X but Y", the answer to a question about what the author recommends is always Y. Options built on X are the standard distractor, since the word does appear in the text.

question: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Twelfth Five Year Plan, the last of the series, was launched in 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Manmohan Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-2017) was launched during the tenure of Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh, and was the last Five Year Plan of India. (बारहवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना — डॉ. मनमोहन सिंह)

 

• Its theme was "Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth", and it set a growth target of 8%, later revised downward.

 

• The Planning Commission, which framed the plans, was set up by an executive resolution in 1950 with the Prime Minister as its ex-officio Chairman. It was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015, and no Thirteenth Plan was framed.

 

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was launched under Jawaharlal Nehru, who was also the first Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. Manmohan Singh was Prime Minister from 2004 to 2014. As Finance Minister under P.V. Narasimha Rao he introduced the LPG reforms of 1991, and he had earlier served as Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and as Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 

• Major legislation of his tenure: the Right to Information Act (2005), MGNREGA (2005), the Right to Education Act (2009) and the National Food Security Act (2013).

 

NOTE

 

• Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Option 1): Prime Minister during the Ninth Plan (1997-2002) and the launch of the Tenth Plan (2002-07).

 

• Narendra Modi (Option 3): Became Prime Minister in 2014, during the currency of the Twelfth Plan, and replaced the Planning Commission with NITI Aayog in 2015.

 

• P.V. Narasimha Rao (Option 4): Prime Minister from 1991 to 1996, during the Eighth Plan.

question: How many Annual Plans were launched during the 'Plan Holiday' between the Third and Fourth Five Year Plans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Three Annual Plans were launched during the "Plan Holiday" of 1966-1969, between the Third and the Fourth Five Year Plans. (योजना अवकाश — तीन वार्षिक योजनाएँ)

 

• The Third Plan (1961-66) had failed because of the Sino-Indian War of 1962, the Indo-Pak War of 1965, a severe drought and famine in 1965-66, and the devaluation of the rupee in 1966. Planning was therefore suspended and the economy managed year by year.

 

• During this period the emphasis was placed firmly on agriculture, and the Green Revolution was launched with high-yielding varieties of seed, chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation.

 

• The Fourth Five Year Plan began in 1969, with the twin objectives of "growth with stability" and the progressive achievement of self-reliance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other interruptions in Indian planning:
◦ The Rolling Plan (1978-1980), introduced by the Janata Government, which terminated the Fifth Plan a year early
◦ Two Annual Plans (1990-92), caused by political instability and the balance of payments crisis, which delayed the Eighth Plan

 

• The Eighth Plan (1992-97) was thus the first plan of the era of liberalisation, and gave a much larger role to the private sector.

 

NOTE

 

• Two (Option 1) is the number of Annual Plans between the Seventh and Eighth Plans, in 1990-92 — the commonest confusion in this question.

 

• Four (Option 3) and Five (Option 4) do not correspond to any period of Indian planning.

question: Which Mughal general was sent by Aurangzeb against Shivaji and concluded the Treaty of Purandar in 1665?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Jai Singh I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mirza Raja Jai Singh I of Amber was sent by Aurangzeb against Shivaji, and concluded the Treaty of Purandar in June 1665. (पुरंदर की संधि — 1665, राजा जय सिंह प्रथम)

 

• Under the treaty:
◦ Shivaji surrendered 23 of his 35 forts, retaining only 12, including Raigad
◦ He agreed to pay tribute and to assist the Mughals in the Deccan
◦ His son Sambhaji was granted a mansab of 5,000 and entered Mughal service

 

• Jai Singh then persuaded Shivaji to visit Agra in 1666, where he was slighted at the court and placed under detention — from which he made his celebrated escape, concealed in baskets of sweetmeats.

 

• Shivaji was formally crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674, and the ceremony was conducted by Gaga Bhatt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shaista Khan, the maternal uncle of Aurangzeb and Governor of the Deccan, was sent against Shivaji in 1660. Shivaji made a daring night attack on his camp at Pune in 1663, in which Shaista Khan lost his fingers and fled.

 

• Earlier, in 1659, Shivaji had killed Afzal Khan, the general of Bijapur, at Pratapgarh.

 

• Shivaji's administration rested on the Ashta Pradhan, a council of eight ministers headed by the Peshwa. His revenue system used the Chauth and Sardeshmukhi levies.

 

NOTE

 

• Shaista Khan (Option 1): Sent in 1660 and defeated at Pune in 1663, but he concluded no treaty.

 

• Dilir Khan (Option 3): A Mughal commander who served under Jai Singh in the Deccan campaigns.

 

• Mirza Raja Man Singh (Option 4): A general of Akbar's reign, who fought at Haldighati in 1576 — a generation earlier.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding soil erosion?

I. Deforestation increases the rate of soil erosion.

II. Contour ploughing helps to check soil erosion on sloping land.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (वनोन्मूलन से मृदा अपरदन बढ़ता है; समोच्च जुताई से यह रुकता है)

 

• Statement I is correct: the roots of trees bind the soil and their canopy breaks the force of falling rain. When forests are cleared, the soil is left exposed to wind and running water, and erosion increases sharply. Overgrazing and shifting cultivation have the same effect.

 

• Statement II is correct: contour ploughing means ploughing along the contours of a slope rather than up and down it. The furrows then run across the direction of flow and act as small barriers, slowing the run-off and allowing water to soak in.

 

• Other methods of checking soil erosion: terrace farming on steep slopes, strip cropping, the planting of shelter belts of trees against wind erosion, afforestation, check dams and gully plugging.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Soil erosion is the removal of the fertile topsoil by wind or water. Severe water erosion produces gullies, and land so cut up is called badland; the ravines of the Chambal are the best-known Indian example.

 

• Major soil types of India: alluvial (the most widespread and fertile), black or regur (best for cotton), red and yellow, laterite, arid, forest and peaty.

 

• The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Bureau of Soil Survey at Nagpur deal with soil classification and conservation.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question: The 'Kalpasutra' and the 'Bhagavati Sutra' belong to which category of ancient Indian literature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jain texts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalpasutra and the Bhagavati Sutra are Jain texts, written in Prakrit (Ardhamagadhi). (कल्पसूत्र एवं भगवती सूत्र — जैन ग्रंथ)

 

• The Kalpasutra was composed by Bhadrabahu and contains the biographies of the Tirthankaras, especially of Mahavira. The Bhagavati Sutra is one of the twelve Angas and gives an account of the life of Mahavira and a list of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.

 

• The Jain canon consists of the 12 Angas, the 12 Upangas, the 10 Prakirnas and other works. It was finally compiled at the Second Jain Council at Valabhi under Devardhi Kshamasramana.

 

• Mahavira preached in Prakrit so that ordinary people might understand him, just as the Buddha preached in Pali.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important texts of the different traditions, frequently asked together:
◦ Buddhist — the Tripitakas (Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma), the Jatakas, the Dhammapada, the Milinda Panho, and the Sri Lankan chronicles Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa
◦ Jain — Kalpasutra, Bhagavati Sutra, Acharanga Sutra, Parishishtaparvan
◦ Vedic — the four Vedas, the Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads
◦ Sangam — Tolkappiyam, Silappadikaram, Manimekalai, Ettuthogai and Pattuppattu

 

NOTE

 

• Buddhist texts (Option 1): The Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa, written in Pali in Sri Lanka, are the best-known examples.

 

• Vedic literature (Option 3): Composed in Sanskrit, and classified as Shruti.

 

• Sangam literature (Option 4): Composed in Tamil in the early centuries of the Christian era.

question: The Krebs cycle, a stage of aerobic respiration, takes place in which part of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Krebs cycle, also called the citric acid cycle or TCA cycle, takes place in the mitochondria of the cell. (क्रेब्स चक्र — माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में)

 

• The stages of aerobic respiration and their locations:
◦ Glycolysis — the breakdown of glucose into pyruvate; occurs in the cytoplasm; yields a net 2 ATP
◦ Krebs cycle — the complete oxidation of pyruvate; occurs in the matrix of the mitochondria; releases carbon dioxide
◦ Electron transport chain (oxidative phosphorylation) — occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane; produces most of the ATP

 

• The complete aerobic oxidation of one molecule of glucose yields about 38 ATP in all, of which the great majority is produced in the mitochondria — which is why they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

 

• The cycle was described by Sir Hans Krebs, who received the Nobel Prize in 1953.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In anaerobic respiration, glycolysis is followed by fermentation in the cytoplasm: in yeast, pyruvate becomes ethanol and carbon dioxide; in our muscles during heavy exercise, it becomes lactic acid, which causes cramp.

 

• Mitochondria have a double membrane, the inner one folded into cristae, and possess their own DNA and ribosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• Cytoplasm (Option 1): The site of glycolysis, the first stage of respiration — the commonest confusion in this question.

 

• Nucleus (Option 3): Contains the DNA and controls the activities of the cell.

 

• Ribosome (Option 4): The site of protein synthesis.

question: Which classical dance form of India is known as the 'dance of the enchantress'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam is known as the "dance of the enchantress". The name comes from Mohini, the female form assumed by Lord Vishnu, and *attam*, meaning dance. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

 

• It belongs to Kerala and is performed solo by women. It is marked by gentle, swaying, circular movements of the body, in contrast to the vigorous style of Kathakali, and its costume is a plain off-white sari with a gold border, the hair gathered in a bun on the left side.

 

• It is accompanied by music in the Sopana style, and its songs are usually in Manipravalam, a mixture of Sanskrit and Malayalam. Swathi Thirunal and Vallathol Narayana Menon, the founder of the Kerala Kalamandalam, did much for its revival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dance forms of India and their states:
◦ Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; the oldest, called the mother of all classical dances
◦ Kathak — Uttar Pradesh; the only one with both Hindu and Mughal influences
◦ Kathakali and Mohiniyattam — Kerala
◦ Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; noted for the Tarangam, danced on the rim of a brass plate
◦ Odissi — Odisha; noted for the tribhanga posture
◦ Manipuri — Manipur; noted for the Raas Leela
◦ Sattriya — Assam; recognised as classical in 2000

 

• All of them derive their theoretical basis from the Natyashastra of Bharata Muni.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): Associated with the temples of Odisha and the Maharis and Gotipuas.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): Takes its name from a village in Andhra Pradesh; traditionally performed by men.

question: 'Jhijhian', a folk dance performed to invoke rain during a drought, belongs to which Indian state?

question: The 'Pushkar Fair', among the largest camel and livestock fairs in the world, is held in which Indian state?

question: The festival of 'Onam', celebrated in Kerala, commemorates the annual visit of which mythical king?

Its features are the Pookalam (floral carpet), the Onasadya (a vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf), the Vallamkali snake-boat race — of which the Nehru Trophy Boat Race on the Punnamada lake is the most famous — and the Pulikali tiger dance and Kaikottikali dance.

question: Which Sikh Guru introduced the concept of 'Miri-Piri' and built the Akal Takht at Amritsar?

• "Miri" stands for temporal or worldly authority and "Piri" for spiritual authority. To symbolise the union of the two, the Guru wore two swords, and taught that the Sikh must be a saint-soldier, combining devotion with the readiness to defend justice.

 

• The Akal Takht, the "Throne of the Timeless One", stands opposite the Harmandir Sahib and is the highest seat of temporal authority for the Sikhs.

 

• This militarisation followed the execution of his father, Guru Arjan Dev, by Jahangir in 1606, and marked a turning point in Sikh history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

◦ Guru Har Rai, Guru Har Krishan — the seventh and eighth Gurus

question: The value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on the Earth is maximum at which of the following?
option_3: At the centre of the Earth
solution_text:
The correct answer is At the poles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The value of the acceleration due to gravity (g) is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator. (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण — ध्रुवों पर अधिकतम)

 

• The reason lies in the shape of the Earth, which is an oblate spheroid — flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator. Since g = GM / R², and the polar radius is smaller than the equatorial radius, g is greater at the poles.
◦ g at the poles ≈ 9.83 m/s²; g at the equator ≈ 9.78 m/s²; the standard value taken is 9.8 m/s².
◦ The rotation of the Earth also reduces the effective value of g at the equator.

 

• Variation of g with position:
◦ It decreases with height above the surface
◦ It decreases with depth below the surface, and becomes zero at the centre of the Earth
◦ On the Moon it is about one-sixth of its value on the Earth

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mass is the quantity of matter in a body and is the same everywhere; weight is the force with which the Earth attracts it, W = mg, and therefore varies from place to place.

 

• A body would weigh nothing at the centre of the Earth, since g is zero there, though its mass would be unchanged.

 

• Newton's law of universal gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂ / r², where G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg² and is constant everywhere in the universe.

 

NOTE

 

• At the equator (Option 1): Here g is at its minimum on the Earth's surface.

 

• At the centre of the Earth (Option 3): Here g is zero.

 

• At a height of 10 km (Option 4): g decreases with height above the surface.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the solar system?

I. Mercury is the smallest planet of the solar system.

II. Venus is the hottest planet of the solar system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (बुध — सबसे छोटा ग्रह; शुक्र — सबसे गर्म ग्रह)

 

• Statement I is correct: Mercury is the smallest planet of the solar system and also the closest to the Sun. It has no atmosphere and no natural satellite, and it completes one revolution in about 88 days — the shortest year of any planet.

 

• Statement II is correct: Venus is the hottest planet, with a surface temperature of about 462°C, although Mercury lies nearer the Sun. The cause is Venus's dense atmosphere of carbon dioxide, which produces a runaway greenhouse effect and traps heat.

 

• Venus is also called the "Morning Star" and "Evening Star", and the "Earth's twin" because of its similar size and mass. It rotates clockwise (retrograde), as does Uranus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Superlatives of the solar system, frequently asked:
◦ Largest planet — Jupiter; smallest — Mercury
◦ Hottest — Venus; coldest — Neptune (Uranus records the lowest temperature)
◦ Densest — Earth; least dense — Saturn, which would float on water
◦ Fastest revolution — Mercury; slowest — Neptune
◦ Most moons — Saturn, with 274 confirmed as of 2025
◦ Red Planet — Mars, which has the largest volcano, Olympus Mons
◦ Planet lying on its side — Uranus

 

• The inner (terrestrial) planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars; the outer (Jovian) planets are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question: Who was the first human being to travel into outer space?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yuri Gagarin.

• Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union became the first human being to travel into outer space on 12 April 1961, aboard the spacecraft Vostok 1. (यूरी गागरिन — अंतरिक्ष में जाने वाले प्रथम मानव)

 

• His flight lasted about 108 minutes and completed one orbit of the Earth. 12 April is observed every year as the International Day of Human Space Flight.

 

• Other landmark "firsts" in space exploration:
◦ First woman in space — Valentina Tereshkova (USSR), Vostok 6, 1963
◦ First person to walk in space — Alexei Leonov (USSR), 1965
◦ First man on the Moon — Neil Armstrong (USA), Apollo 11, 20 July 1969, accompanied by Buzz Aldrin, with Michael Collins in the command module
◦ First American in space — Alan Shepard, 1961
◦ First artificial satellite — Sputnik 1 (USSR), 1957

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

• India's human spaceflight programme is Gaganyaan, and 23 August is observed as National Space Day, marking the landing of Chandrayaan-3.

question: The 'Bihu geet' of Assam are associated chiefly with which season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bihu geet are associated chiefly with spring, and are sung during Rongali (Bohag) Bihu, celebrated in the month of Bohag (April) to mark the Assamese new year and the beginning of the sowing season. (बिहू गीत — वसंत ऋतु, असम)

 

• The songs are lively and are accompanied by the dhol, the pepa (a horn pipe made from buffalo horn), the gogona, the taal and the toka, and are performed with the Bihu dance by young men and women.

 

• Assam has three Bihus:
◦ Rongali or Bohag Bihu — April; the spring festival and the new year, and the most joyous of the three
◦ Bhogali or Magh Bihu — January; the harvest festival, marked by feasting and the burning of the *meji*
◦ Kongali or Kati Bihu — October; an austere occasion when the granaries are empty and lamps are lit before the tulsi plant

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk songs and dances of Assam: Bagurumba (the butterfly dance of the Bodos), Jhumur (of the tea tribes), Ojapali, Borgeet (devotional songs composed by Srimanta Sankardeva) and Ankiya Nat, from which the classical Sattriya dance developed.

 

• Seasonal folk songs of other regions: Kajari (rainy season, Uttar Pradesh), Chaiti (the month of Chaitra), Barahmasa (the twelve months) and Basant songs of spring.

 

NOTE

 

• Monsoon (Option 2): The season of the Kajari songs of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

 

• Autumn (Option 3): The season of Kati Bihu, but that is an austere observance with few songs of this kind.

 

• Winter (Option 4): The season of Magh Bihu, the harvest festival, which is marked chiefly by feasting.

question: A car moving with a velocity of 72 km/h is brought to rest in 5 seconds. Calculate the retardation of the car (in m/s²).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Given: initial velocity u = 72 km/h; final velocity v = 0 (the car comes to rest); time t = 5 s.

 

• Step 1 — Convert the velocity to SI units.
◦ To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by 5/18.
◦ u = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s

 

• Step 2 — Apply the first equation of motion.
◦ v = u + at
◦ 0 = 20 + a × 5
◦ a = −20 ÷ 5 = −4 m/s²

 

• The negative sign shows that the velocity is decreasing. The magnitude of this negative acceleration is called retardation or deceleration, and is therefore 4 m/s².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three equations of motion for uniform acceleration:
◦ v = u + at
◦ s = ut + ½at²
◦ v² = u² + 2as

 

• Useful conversions: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s, and 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h. Forgetting this conversion is the commonest source of error in such questions.

 

• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, its SI unit is m/s², and it is a vector quantity.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 m/s² (Option 1) would result from taking u as 10 m/s.

 

• 3 m/s² (Option 2) and 5 m/s² (Option 4) do not follow from the given data. Note that a candidate who forgets the conversion and divides 72 by 5 obtains 14.4, which appears among none of the options — a warning that the conversion has been missed.

question: India joined the Mineral Security Partnership (MSP), an initiative to secure critical mineral supply chains, in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India joined the Mineral Security Partnership (MSP) in June 2023, becoming its fourteenth member. (खनिज सुरक्षा भागीदारी — भारत 2023 में शामिल)

 

• The MSP was launched in June 2022 on the initiative of the United States. Its purpose is to secure critical mineral supply chains and to reduce the concentration of their production and processing in a few countries.

 

• Its members include the United States, Australia, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, South Korea, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Italy, Estonia and the European Commission.

 

• Critical minerals are those essential to modern technology and to the energy transition, and whose supply is at risk — lithium, cobalt, nickel, graphite, rare earth elements and others. They are indispensable for electric vehicle batteries, semiconductors, solar panels and wind turbines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India released its list of 30 critical minerals in 2023, and the Ministry of Mines has begun the auction of critical mineral blocks. The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023 permits private participation in the exploration of these minerals.

 

• KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Limited), a joint venture of three public sector undertakings, was set up in 2019 to acquire mineral assets abroad.

 

• India is heavily dependent on imports for lithium and cobalt. A significant lithium deposit was reported in the Reasi district of Jammu & Kashmir in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• 2021 (Option 1): The MSP did not exist in this year.

 

• 2022 (Option 2): The year the MSP itself was launched, a year before India joined — the commonest confusion in this question.

 

• 2024 (Option 4): By this year India had already been a member for a year.

question: Which institution is responsible for the regulation of the securities market in India?
option_2: Securities and Exchange Board of India
option_3: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
option_4: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
solution_text:

• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulator of the securities market in India. (सेबी — प्रतिभूति बाजार का नियामक)

 

• It was constituted as a non-statutory body in 1988 and given statutory status by the SEBI Act, 1992, its creation being hastened by the Harshad Mehta securities scam of that year. Its headquarters is at Mumbai, and it functions under the Ministry of Finance.

 

• Its three stated objectives are:
◦ To protect the interests of investors in securities
◦ To promote the development of the securities market
◦ To regulate the securities market

 

• SEBI exercises quasi-legislative, quasi-executive and quasi-judicial powers — it frames regulations, conducts investigations and passes orders. Appeals against its decisions lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's financial regulators and their domains:
◦ RBI (1935) — banking, currency and monetary policy; it controls the money supply
◦ SEBI (1992) — the securities market
◦ IRDAI (1999) — insurance; headquarters at Hyderabad
◦ PFRDA (2013) — pensions
◦ NABARD (1982) — agriculture and rural credit
◦ IBBI (2016) — insolvency and bankruptcy

 

• India's two principal stock exchanges are the BSE (1875), the oldest in Asia, whose index is the Sensex of 30 companies, and the NSE (1992), whose index is the Nifty 50.

 

NOTE

 

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 1): Regulates banking and controls the money supply, not the securities market.

 

• NABARD (Option 3): The apex bank for agriculture and rural development.

 

• IRDAI (Option 4): Regulates the insurance sector.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding mineral resources in India?

I. India has to import a large part of its requirement of crude petroleum.

II. India is largely self-sufficient in iron ore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (कच्चे तेल में भारत आयात पर निर्भर; लौह अयस्क में आत्मनिर्भर)

 

• Statement I is correct: India imports well over 80% of its requirement of crude petroleum, which makes it the largest single item in the country's import bill and a major influence on its balance of payments and on inflation.

 

• Statement II is correct: India is largely self-sufficient in iron ore and is in fact a net exporter of it. India has among the largest reserves of haematite in the world, and Odisha is the largest producing state, followed by Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Jharkhand.

 

• India's mineral position in brief:
◦ Self-sufficient or surplus — iron ore, bauxite, chromite, manganese, limestone, mica, coal (in quantity, though not in coking quality)
◦ Deficient and largely imported — crude petroleum, coking coal, copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt and rare earth elements

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

• India's oil fields: Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran (Assam), Ankleshwar and Kalol (Gujarat), Mumbai High (offshore, the largest producer), Barmer (Rajasthan) and the Krishna-Godavari basin.

 

• The Indian Bureau of Mines at Nagpur publishes the Indian Minerals Yearbook, and the Geological Survey of India, founded in 1851 with headquarters at Kolkata, carries out mineral exploration.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question: Who is the author of the novel 'The Inheritance of Loss', which won the Booker Prize in 2006?
solution_text:

• "The Inheritance of Loss" (2006) was written by Kiran Desai, and won the Man Booker Prize in 2006. (द इनहेरिटेंस ऑफ लॉस — किरण देसाई)

question: Who is the author of the book 'Sita: An Illustrated Retelling of the Ramayana'?

• Note that two different books called "Sita" are frequently confused in examinations: Devdutt Pattanaik's illustrated retelling and Amish Tripathi's novel "Sita: Warrior of Mithila".

 

NOTE

 

• Amish Tripathi (Option 2): Author of *Sita: Warrior of Mithila*, the second book of the Ram Chandra Series.

 

• Anand Neelakantan (Option 3): Author of *Asura*, which retells the Ramayana from Ravana's point of view.

 

• Ashwin Sanghi (Option 4): Author of historical and mythological thrillers.

question: The 'Vijay Stambh' (Tower of Victory) at Chittorgarh was built by which ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rana Kumbha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vijay Stambh, or Tower of Victory, at Chittorgarh was built by Rana Kumbha between 1440 and 1448 to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa. (विजय स्तंभ — राणा कुंभा)

 

• It is about 37 metres high, has nine storeys, and is covered with sculptures of Hindu deities, which has led to its being described as a museum of Indian sculpture.

 

• Standing near it is the older Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame), a 22-metre, seven-storeyed tower built in the twelfth century by a Jain merchant and dedicated to Adinatha, the first Tirthankara.

 

• Chittorgarh Fort is the largest fort in India and one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013, along with Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rana Kumbha (1433-1468) of Mewar was a great builder and is credited with 32 of the 84 forts of Mewar, including Kumbhalgarh, whose wall is among the longest in the world. He was also a scholar and musician, and wrote the "Sangit Raj".

 

• The three jauhars of Chittor are traditionally dated to 1303 (Alauddin Khalji, in the time of Rana Ratan Singh and Rani Padmini), 1535 (Bahadur Shah of Gujarat) and 1568 (Akbar, defended by Jaimal and Patta).

 

NOTE

 

• Rana Sanga (Option 2): Defeated by Babur at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

 

• Rana Pratap (Option 3): Fought Akbar at Haldighati in 1576.

 

• Rana Ratan Singh (Option 4): The ruler at the time of Alauddin Khalji's siege of Chittor in 1303.

question: The Agra Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built by which Mughal emperor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Agra Fort was built by Akbar between 1565 and 1573, chiefly of red sandstone from Rajasthan. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. (आगरा का किला — अकबर)

 

• It stands on the bank of the Yamuna and is crescent-shaped, with a double wall about 2.5 km in circumference. Its principal gates are the Delhi Gate and the Amar Singh Gate.

 

• Later emperors added to it. Shah Jahan built the Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, Khas Mahal, Sheesh Mahal, Musamman Burj and the white marble Moti Masjid within its walls. Shah Jahan spent his last years imprisoned in the fort by Aurangzeb, with a view of the Taj Mahal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mughal architecture and its builders:
◦ Akbar — Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri with the Buland Darwaza, Lahore Fort; his own tomb at Sikandra was completed by Jahangir
◦ Jahangir — chiefly gardens, such as Shalimar Bagh in Kashmir; the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula was built by Nur Jahan
◦ Shah Jahan — the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid at Delhi, and the Moti Masjid at Agra
◦ Aurangzeb — the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, Delhi, and the Badshahi Mosque at Lahore

 

• Akbar's reign (1556-1605) also saw the Mansabdari system, the Dahsala revenue settlement of Raja Todar Mal, and the doctrine of Sulh-i-Kul.

 

NOTE

 

• Jahangir (Option 2): Remembered more for painting and gardens than for building.

 

• Shah Jahan (Option 3): Added the marble palaces within the fort, but did not build the fort itself.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): Imprisoned his father within the fort but added little to it.

question: Which metal is commonly used for galvanising iron in order to prevent it from rusting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zinc.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Galvanisation is the process of coating iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc to protect it from rusting. (जस्तीकरण — लोहे पर जस्ते की परत)

 

• Zinc protects the iron in two ways:
◦ It forms a physical barrier between the iron and the moist air
◦ It is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes in preference to the iron even if the coating is scratched. This is called sacrificial protection.

 

• Rusting is the slow oxidation of iron in the presence of both oxygen and moisture, producing hydrated iron oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O). Rust is flaky and does not protect the metal beneath, so corrosion continues.

 

• Galvanised iron is used for roofing sheets, water pipes, buckets and nails.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other methods of preventing rusting: painting, greasing and oiling, electroplating, anodising (for aluminium), alloying (as in stainless steel, an alloy of iron with chromium and nickel) and cathodic protection.

 

• Related processes frequently asked:
◦ Electroplating — depositing a layer of one metal on another by electrolysis; silver and gold are used on cheaper metals for ornaments, and chromium on car parts
◦ Tinning — coating with tin, used for food cans, since tin is unreactive and non-toxic

 

• Zinc's ores are zinc blende (ZnS) and calamine; Rajasthan is India's principal producer.

 

NOTE

 

• Copper (Option 2): Being less reactive than iron, it would accelerate corrosion of the iron if the coating were broken.

 

• Tin (Option 3): Used in tinning food cans, not in galvanisation.

 

• Lead (Option 4): Toxic, and not used for this purpose.
